Display an image or a matrix

Source: R/express-imshow.R
px_imshow.Rd

Displays a matrix as a heatmap, or an RGB/RGBA array as an image, like plotly.py's px.imshow(). Higher-dimensional arrays can be split into facets and animation frames with facet_col, facet_row and animation_frame.

Usage

px_imshow(
  img,
  zmin = NULL,
  zmax = NULL,
  origin = NULL,
  labels = list(),
  x = NULL,
  y = NULL,
  animation_frame = NULL,
  facet_col = NULL,
  facet_row = NULL,
  facet_col_wrap = NULL,
  facet_col_spacing = NULL,
  facet_row_spacing = NULL,
  color_continuous_scale = NULL,
  color_continuous_midpoint = NULL,
  range_color = NULL,
  title = NULL,
  template = NULL,
  width = NULL,
  height = NULL,
  aspect = NULL,
  contrast_rescaling = NULL,
  binary_string = NULL,
  binary_backend = "auto",
  binary_compression_level = 4,
  binary_format = "png",
  text_auto = FALSE
)

Arguments

img

The image: a numeric or logical matrix (shown as a heatmap with a continuous color scale), a data.frame (its column and row names give x and y), or an array of dimension c(height, width, 3) (RGB) or c(height, width, 4) (RGBA) shown as an image. Raw vectors and integer arrays with values 0-255 are treated as 8-bit images; numeric images are scaled according to their range (e.g. 0-1 for png::readPNG() output). With facet_col, facet_row or animation_frame, one more dimension per argument.

zmin, zmax

Minimum and maximum of the color range (per channel for RGB(A) images: a single value, or 1, 3 or 4 values).

origin

"upper" (default, row 1 at the top) or "lower".

labels

Named list overriding the labels of x, y, color, facet_col, facet_row and animation_frame.

x, y

Coordinates of the columns and rows (numeric for RGB images).

animation_frame, facet_col, facet_row

Dimension of img (a number, or a name in names(dimnames(img))) to split into animation frames, facet columns or facet rows.

facet_col_wrap

Maximum number of facet columns.

facet_col_spacing, facet_row_spacing

Spacing between facets, as a fraction of the figure.

color_continuous_scale, color_continuous_midpoint, range_color

Color scale settings for single-channel images (see px_args).

title, template, width, height

See px_args.

aspect

"equal" (default for arrays; square pixels) or "auto" (fill the figure).

contrast_rescaling

"minmax" (scale to the data range; default for single-channel images) or "infer" (scale to the range implied by the data type).

binary_string

If TRUE, RGB(A) images are sent as a compressed PNG (needs the png package) instead of an array of values; the default when png is installed.

binary_backend, binary_compression_level

Unused; accepted for compatibility with plotly.py.

binary_format

Only "png" is supported.

text_auto

If TRUE or a d3-format string, show the values as text on heatmaps.

Value

A go_figure().

See also

Other plotly express: px_area(), px_bar(), px_bar_polar(), px_box(), px_choropleth(), px_choropleth_map(), px_density_contour(), px_density_heatmap(), px_density_map(), px_ecdf(), px_funnel(), px_funnel_area(), px_histogram(), px_icicle(), px_line(), px_line_3d(), px_line_geo(), px_line_map(), px_line_polar(), px_line_ternary(), px_parallel_categories(), px_parallel_coordinates(), px_pie(), px_scatter(), px_scatter_3d(), px_scatter_geo(), px_scatter_map(), px_scatter_matrix(), px_scatter_polar(), px_scatter_ternary(), px_strip(), px_sunburst(), px_timeline(), px_treemap(), px_violin()

Examples

px_imshow(matrix(c(1, 20, 30, 20, 1, 60, 30, 60, 1), 3), text_auto = TRUE)

img <- array(c(255, 0, 0, 0, 255, 0, 0, 0, 255, 255, 255, 0), dim = c(2, 2, 3))
px_imshow(img, binary_string = FALSE)

volume <- array(stats::runif(5 * 20 * 20), dim = c(5, 20, 20))
px_imshow(volume, animation_frame = 1)
